# Wesen (essence) - chronological ledger

*Generated by `scripts/synthesis_ledger.py` from `synthesis/extractions/wesen/`. Do not edit by hand - edit the extraction records and rebuild.*

*Descartes' vera et immutabilis natura (Meditation V) and Husserl's Wesen/eidos both do the same anti-nominalist work — an essence's necessary properties hold independently of any existing instance — but Descartes secures it theologically (the eternal truths as God's creation) where Husserl secures it by eidetic intuition alone. Opened from a cross-corpus question about whether Husserl treats 'true and immutable natures' as a phenomenological residuum; no commentary in the corpus yet states the connection explicitly, see gap-007.*

4 units and 1 recorded absences from 1 commentaries.

## Reception layer

*Read alongside the spine, not on it. A commentator's date orders the reception, not the doctrine.*

### 1986 - Jean-Luc Marion, Sur le prisme métaphysique de Descartes — Commentary

`marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary`

- **introduced** · `wesen/marion-prisme/001` · *innate idea*
  The idea of God in the fifth Meditation is presented as an innate idea drawn from the same reserve of thought as every other innate idea, not from experience.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-20-the-name-out-of-play` · [§ 20. The Name Out of Play](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-name-out-of-play)
  > exactly as all the innate ideas are drawn from thought, the idea of God is drawn from the reserve where, among others, it was as it were stocked

- **introduced** · `wesen/marion-prisme/002` · *true and immutable natures*
  Innate ideas are said to offer their true and immutable natures, each attesting a determinate nature, essence or form of it, immutable and eternal.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-20-the-name-out-of-play` · [§ 20. The Name Out of Play](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-name-out-of-play)
  > namely all those that offer their true and immutable natures and so attest a certain determinate nature or essence or form of it, immutable and eternal

- **introduced** · `wesen/marion-prisme/003` · *figure*
  Marion states that the idea of God is found in the mind no less than the idea of a triangle, placing it among the simple natures of extension, figure and number.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-20-the-name-out-of-play` · [§ 20. The Name Out of Play](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-name-out-of-play)
  > the idea of God is found in me no less, that is, at most as much, as the idea of a triangle, and so as the simple natures of extension, figure, number

- **criticized** · `wesen/marion-prisme/004` · *true and immutable natures*
  Because determination [B], God as supremely perfect, shares the epistemic status of the true-and-immutable simple natures, Marion concludes it contradicts determination [A], God as incomprehensible infinite.
  `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-20-the-name-out-of-play` · [§ 20. The Name Out of Play](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#the-name-out-of-play)
  > it must definitively be admitted that [A] and [B] contradict one another on the parameter of incomprehensibility

#### Recorded absences

- **absent** · `marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary#h3-s-6-a-nothing-of-ontology`
  Expected because: This passage treats an extended geometrical figure at length as an object the mind reduces to a minimal ens (Rule XIV's figuratum: body, surface, line, point) - the same kind of geometrical object that section 20 later calls a true and immutable nature - yet describes it only as an ens 'respectu intellectus nostri', without the immutable-nature vocabulary.
  The passage uses essentia and figure extensively but never pairs geometrical figure with immutable-nature vocabulary; that pairing appears only later, at section 20, once Marion turns to the fifth Meditation.
  [§ 6. A Nothing of Ontology](https://faultynode.github.io/commentaries/commentaries/marion/marion-sur-le-prisme-metaphysique-de-descartes-commentary.html#a-nothing-of-ontology)

*Partial pass: Covers chapter II §6 (p. 80-82, the Rule XIV figuratum passage) and chapter IV §20 (pp. 276-281, the fifth-Meditation 'true and immutable natures' passage) in full. Chapter I (§§1-5, pp. 1-72), the ego/substance material of chapter III not already read (roughly pp. 160-176), and chapter V (Pascal, pp. 296-324) were only keyword-scanned for the theme's search terms, not read paragraph by paragraph.*
